text: A windfall is a large amount of money you did not expect or work for, like fruit blown off a tree by the wind. Here it is the money America pays the Marshall Islands.
A supplement is something added to what you already have. Here the payment would be extra money on top of wages.
Cumbersome means slow, clumsy and awkward because there is too much to do. Checking who qualifies would take a lot of work.
An arsenal is a country's stock of weapons. A nuclear arsenal is its collection of nuclear bombs.
An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island that surrounds a calm lagoon of water.
Administered means run or managed. The islands were once managed by America.
Scattered means spread out over a wide area, not close together.
Radiation is invisible energy given off by nuclear material. A lot of it can seriously harm the body.
Lasting means continuing for a very long time.
Marshallese means the people of the Marshall Islands, or relating to them.
A compact is a formal agreement. Under this one, America gives money and the islands allow American military access.
In exchange for means giving one thing to get another, like a trade.
To be enrolled is to be signed up on an official list.
Quarterly means once every three months, so four times a year.
A citizen is a person who officially belongs to a country and has its rights.
Universal basic income, or UBI, means the government gives every person the same regular payment, with no conditions. Universal means for everyone.
Unconditional means with no rules or strings attached. You do not have to do anything to get it.
Wages are the money people are paid for their work.
An architect designs buildings. Here it means the person who came up with the plan.
Peace of mind means feeling calm because you are not worried.
The cost of living is how much money people need for basics like food, housing and clothes.
To insist is to say something very firmly and refuse to change your mind.
Labour supply is how many people are willing to work. People might work less if they get free money.
An economist is an expert who studies how money, jobs and prices work.
Consumption means how much people buy and use. When they spend more, consumption goes up.
The labour force is all the people who have jobs or are looking for one.
A cheque is a printed paper that tells a bank to pay money to the person named on it.
Inflation is when prices across a whole economy rise over time, so the same money buys less.
A cash transfer is money the government gives straight to people.
To attribute something to a cause means to say that cause made it happen.
Remote means far away from other places and hard to reach.
An obstacle is something that blocks your way or makes a goal harder.
Whopping is an informal word for very large.
GDP, gross domestic product, is the total value of everything made and sold in a country in one year. Percent of GDP shows how big a cost is for that country.
A trust fund is a pile of money set aside and managed for a special purpose.
The IMF, or International Monetary Fund, is a group of countries that lends money and gives economic advice.
Infrastructure means the basic things a place needs to work, like roads, bridges, ports and power lines.
Climate adaptation means changing how we live to cope with a changing climate, like building sea walls.
A targeted scheme gives help only to some chosen people, not everyone.
Feasible means possible to do.
To qualify is to meet the rules needed to get something.
Remittances are money that people working in another country send home to their families.
Vulnerable means easy to hurt or damage.
An economic shock is a sudden event, like a war or disaster, that hurts the economy.
Social protection means programs that help people in need, like food help or unemployment money.
An evaluation is a careful study that checks whether something worked.
Job displacement is when people lose jobs because something else, like a machine, takes their place.
Artificial intelligence, or AI, is computer technology that can do tasks that normally need human thinking.
A centrist group has political views in the middle, not strongly left or right.
Lessons here means useful things other people can learn from the experiment.
